d: Venue-wide preferences, plus a few settings that change how MomentusMAX behaves.
b: Currency, regional format, date format, fiscal year start month, and time zone.
Opportunity Inactivity sets how many days without activity before MomentusMAX creates a follow-up task.
The fiscal year start month is permanent once it is saved.
r: Admins can change it. Sales managers and reps can open it but cannot change anything.

d: Add users, assign or change a role, and remove access.
b: The three roles are Sales Rep, Sales Manager, and Admin.
Changes take effect on the user's next login.
MomentusMAX always keeps at least one Admin.

d: How the interactive calendar opens and behaves for everyone in your organization.
b: Defaults set the opening view, the first day of the week, and the working-hour window.
Venue closures stop anyone from placing holds on those dates.
Changes apply the next time someone loads a calendar.

d: Shows the MomentusMAX credits your account has used, by day and by kind of work.
b: It is for visibility only. No usage limits are enforced yet.
Choose a period, such as This month or Last 3 months, to change the view.
Credits are grouped into categories, such as communication and space planning.

d: Your venue's revenue targets. MomentusMAX measures pipeline and bookings against these.
b: Three tabs: Prior Years, This Year, and Future Years.
Set the target at the annual, quarterly, or monthly level.
Your first saved goal is the baseline. Use Re-forecast to change it later.

d: Each representative's share of the venue target, at annual, quarterly, and monthly level.
b: A summary card compares the venue total with what you have assigned.
Assign Target puts the table into edit mode.
Over-assigning and under-assigning are both allowed.
r: Hidden from sales reps. Admins and sales managers can see it.

d: Controls which price list MomentusMAX suggests first. It does not restrict what a rep can choose.
b: Drag lists to reorder them. The top list in each section is suggested first.
Three scopes: Holds, Packages & Services, and Everywhere as the fallback.
A list marked Unavailable was removed or deactivated in your source system.
r: Admins can edit. Sales managers can view only. Reps cannot see it.

d: Set the default look for proposals and manage your library of uploaded templates.
b: Defaults cover the logo, its placement, the primary color, and the cover page style.
Upload a PDF to turn it into a template, then map its fields to opportunity data.
Only Published templates can be chosen when a rep builds a proposal.

d: Defines how MomentusMAX scores every opportunity on value, win probability, and urgency.
b: Four tabs: Score Display, Value, Probability, and Urgency.
Score Display sets the red, yellow, and green bands, and how the three scores combine.
Every setting starts with a default, so scoring works from day one.
r: Hidden from sales reps. Sales managers can view it. Admins can edit.

d: Configure how past events are matched to new inquiries to get space plan recommendations.
b: Eligible Events controls how much of your event history can be used.
Scoring Factors set how much each factor counts and how different a past event can be.
Live Preview tests a sample inquiry against your history.

d: Sets the day thresholds behind reply badges and the automatic follow-up tasks that go with them.
b: Warning threshold: how long an unanswered outbound message waits before an amber badge.
Critical threshold: when the badge turns red. It must be greater than the warning threshold.
Customer awaiting reply after: how long a customer message can sit unanswered.

d: The written guidance the AI follows when it drafts emails, captures notes, and recommends spaces.
b: Four tabs: Venue, Email, Spaces, and Notes. Each feeds a different part of the AI's output.
Write instructions once for your venue, and the AI follows them from then on.
New instruction adds one, and you open it from the list to edit.

d: Lists records held in your source system and lets you choose which to bring into MomentusMAX. Nothing imports on its own.
b: Tabs for Events, Event Opportunities, and Opportunities.
Filter the list, select the rows you want, then choose Import Selected.
Complete the mapping screens first, because import matching depends on them.

d: Matches event types from your source system to Momentus reporting types.
b: The reporting type is what analytics and goal tracking count.
The Needs mapping count shows reporting types with nothing assigned yet.
Sync Event Types pulls the current list from your source system.

d: Maps your Enterprise note classes to note categories. The menu item says Notes Class Mapping, and the screen is titled Note Class Mapping.
b: MomentusMAX uses the mapping when AI generates a note and when a note skill creates one.
Sync Note Classes pulls the current class list from Enterprise.
Choose No mapping to leave a category unmapped.

d: Connects your organization's Microsoft account so email and meeting invitations attach to the right opportunity automatically.
b: Connect the organization first, then choose which mailboxes sync.
Domain Exclusions keeps internal mail out of MomentusMAX.
The connection is read-only. MomentusMAX never sends mail from it.

d: Teaches MomentusMAX to look past no-reply and automated addresses to find the real contact.
b: Each pattern is an address to catch, and * works as a wildcard.
The platform name is optional and helps you tell entries apart.
Use it when inquiries from a lead source arrive with the wrong contact.

d: Your own account details, not your organization's.
b: Shows your assigned role, with a link to view what that role can do.
Email Signatures are the signatures available when you write an email.

d: Your own display, time, and appearance preferences, not your organization's.
b: Choose the language for the interface and the language for AI-drafted email.
Appearance can be Light, Dark, or System.
Your time zone changes how times are shown to you.

d: Shows Company Background usage, including the number of requests used.
b: Two tabs: Usage and Status Lookup.
Filter the usage by month and year.

d: Controls which bookings hold a space in MomentusMAX.
b: Bookings are grouped by status code into Open, Tentative, Definite, Cancelled, Lost, and Archived.
Cancelled, Lost, and Archived bookings never hold a space.
Your booking statuses lists every status, and a status set individually overrides its category.
r: Choose carefully: this changes what every rep sees as available.
